terms.meaning: a call where the top two options are too close to call

sections.name: File setup, CalibrationStatus, Grade
sections.title: Setup, band size and grade shape
sections.what: Sets the coin-flip band at 2 points, imports the decision type, and describes a grade: points, coin-flip flag, best option, and a calibration status that is always provisional.
sections.why: Likely reason: a fixed band and a provisional tag, as the comments state.
sections.watch_out: The 2-point band is a fixed choice, and changing it changes which calls go ungraded.

sections.name: grade
sections.title: Grading one pick
sections.what: Checks there are at least two options, that the pick exists, and that every win chance is between 0 and 1. Finds the best option, marks a coin flip when the top two are within 2 points, and returns the pick's gap to the best other option in points.
sections.why: Likely reason: grading against the best alternative measures the decision.
sections.watch_out: Ties at the top are not handled specially, so which option is named best can depend on order.

sections.name: gradeDecision
sections.title: Grading a moment's decision
sections.what: Takes a moment's decision. If it has too little data it returns nothing. Otherwise passes its option chances to the grader.
sections.why: Likely reason: avoids grading decisions that the data cannot support.
sections.watch_out: Callers must check for nothing, or they will fail on an ungraded moment.

summary: Turns the win chances of each option into a grade for a pick: how many points better or worse it was than the best alternative, and whether the call was too close to grade.
purpose: Grades the decision rather than the result, so a good call that lost still scores well.
why: The header says to grade the decision, not the outcome. The calibration note says grades are provisional while calibration is a known issue.
how: Checks the options, finds the best option and the gap between the top two, marks a coin flip if that gap is under 2 points, and computes the pick's chance minus the best of the others. For a moment, passes its options through, or returns nothing if it has too little data.
inputs: A map from each option to its win chance, plus the pick. For a moment, the decision with its options.
outputs: A grade with points, the coin-flip flag, the best option and a provisional tag. Or nothing when the moment is not graded.
risks: Grades are provisional because calibration is a known issue. Nothing is returned for insufficient data, so callers must handle that case.
debug: If a grade is missing, check the insufficient flag. If a points value looks odd, check that win chances are between 0 and 1 and that the pick name matches an option exactly.
